**Ludora - the Client for all Game Clients** · Release 0.8.9

### What's new
- **Your own launchers find their games by themselves.** Add a launcher with just its program and Ludora looks for the games: in the launcher's data folders, in the install paths from its settings files, in Windows "Apps & features" and one level deeper for games like Xbox or Oculus titles. If nothing is found, the launcher itself shows up as a game so it's never empty.
- **Minecraft launchers:** instances and profiles show up as games – official launcher and TLauncher profiles, Prism, PolyMC, MultiMC and ATLauncher (started directly), CurseForge, Modrinth, FTB, GDLauncher, Technic and NoRisk (open the launcher).
- **Sidebar:** all numbers, the downloads percentage and the open/download buttons line up on the right.

### Updating
Just click the update button as usual. Settings, sign-ins and covers stay.

### Downloads
| System | File |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 | `Ludora-Setup-0.8.9.exe` |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `Ludora-0.8.9-arm64.dmg` (or `.zip`) |
| macOS (Intel) | `Ludora-0.8.9-x64.dmg` (or `.zip`) |
| Linux (any distribution) | `Ludora-0.8.9-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Debian / Ubuntu | `Ludora-0.8.9-amd64.deb` |

The files are not code-signed: on Windows click **More info → Run anyway**, on macOS **right-click → Open** on the first start.

**Deutsch:** Eigene Launcher finden ihre Spiele jetzt selbst – in ihren Datenordnern, über die Installationspfade aus ihren Einstellungen, über „Apps & Features“ und eine Ebene tiefer (z. B. Xbox). Minecraft-Launcher zeigen ihre Instanzen und Profile als Spiele (offizieller Launcher, TLauncher, Prism, MultiMC, ATLauncher, CurseForge, Modrinth, FTB, GDLauncher, Technic, NoRisk). Findet Ludora nichts, steht der Launcher selbst als Spiel da. In der Seitenleiste sind alle Zahlen und Knöpfe rechts bündig. Update wie gewohnt über den Update-Knopf.
